Certainty Silhouette Width (CeS) for Soft Clustering

Source: R/cerSilhouette.R
cerSilhouette.Rd

Computes the certainty silhouette (CeS) of Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika (2024) for each observation: the membership probability of its assigned cluster (by default, its largest membership).

Usage

cerSilhouette(
  prob_matrix,
  average = c("crisp", "fuzzy", "median"),
  a = 2,
  sort = FALSE,
  print.summary = FALSE,
  clust_fun = NULL,
  ...,
  cluster = NULL,
  clust_args = list()
)

Arguments

prob_matrix

A numeric matrix of posterior probabilities where rows represent observations and columns represent clusters. Must sum to 1 by row. If clust_fun is provided, prob_matrix must be a string giving the name of the matrix component (e.g., "u").

average

Character string specifying the method for computing the average silhouette width. Options are:

  • "crisp" – unweighted (simple) average.

  • "fuzzy" – weighted average; the weight of an observation is the gap between its two largest memberships raised to the power a.

  • "median" – median silhouette width across observations.

Defaults to "crisp".

a

Non-negative number, the exponent \(\alpha\) of the weights in fuzzy silhouette averaging. Higher values increase the emphasis on strong membership differences; a = 0 gives every observation the same weight, so the fuzzy average equals the crisp average. Defaults to 2.

sort

Logical; if TRUE, sorts the output widths data frame by cluster and descending silhouette width. Defaults to FALSE.

print.summary

Logical; if TRUE, reports a summary table of average silhouette widths and sizes for each cluster through message. Defaults to FALSE for Silhouette() and TRUE for summary().

clust_fun

Optional S3 or S4 function object or function as character string specifying a clustering function that produces the membership matrix. For example, fcm or "fcm". If provided, prob_matrix must be a string giving the name of the matrix component (e.g., "u"). Defaults to NULL.

...

Additional arguments passed to clust_fun, such as x, centers for fcm.

cluster

Optional integer vector of length \(n\) giving the cluster of each observation as a column number of prob_matrix. If NULL (the default), each observation is assigned to the cluster with its largest membership (for "pp" and "nlpp") or its largest density (for "pd"); see Cluster labels. If clust_fun is provided, cluster may be the name of the label component of its output. Must be named in the call because it follows ....

clust_args

A list of further arguments for clust_fun; use it for arguments whose names could be partially matched to this function's own (for example clust_args = list(m = 3) for the fuzzifier of fcm). Defaults to list().

Value

A data frame of class "Silhouette" with one row per observation and columns cluster, neighbor, weight (only when average = "fuzzy") and sil_width. The object includes the following attributes:

proximity_type

The proximity type used i.e., "similarity".

method

The silhouette calculation method used i.e., "certainty".

average

Character — the averaging method: "crisp", "fuzzy", or "median".

Details

The certainty silhouette is the counterpart of the uncertainty used in model-based clustering: values near 1 indicate high certainty that an observation belongs to its cluster, and values near \(1/K\) ambiguity. It is bounded below by \(1/K\), so its level falls as \(K\) grows; Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika (2024) read the number of clusters from the reverse elbow drop of its average over \(k\) (see softSilhouette).

Let the posterior probability matrix or cluster membership matrix be \(\Gamma = [\gamma_{ik}]_{n \times K}\). The certainty silhouette width for observation \(i\) assigned to cluster \(c_i\) is: $$ \mathrm{Cer}_i = \gamma_{ic_i}, $$ which equals \(\max_{k} \gamma_{ik} \in [1/K, 1]\) with the default labels. With labels supplied through cluster, the width lies in \([0, 1]\). The neighbor column gives the cluster with the largest membership other than \(c_i\).

Ties are resolved in favor of the first column; see Silhouette.

Averages

If average = "crisp", the crisp silhouette index (\(CS\)) is the mean width: $$ CS = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} S(x_i) $$ summarizing overall clustering quality.

If average = "fuzzy" and prob_matrix is provided, denoted as \(\Gamma = [\gamma_{ik}]_{n \times K}\), with \(\gamma_{ik}\) representing the probability of observation \(i\) belonging to cluster \(k\), the fuzzy silhouette index (\(FS\)) of Campello and Hruschka (2006) is: $$ FS = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i S(x_i) }{\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i}, \qquad w_i = ( \gamma_{i(1)} - \gamma_{i(2)} )^{\alpha}, $$ where \(\gamma_{i(1)}\) and \(\gamma_{i(2)}\) are the largest and second largest memberships of observation \(i\), and \(\alpha\) (the a argument) controls the emphasis on confident assignments (\(\alpha \ge 0\); \(\alpha = 0\) gives the crisp average). The weight \(w_i\) is stored in the weight column and does not depend on the cluster labels; it equals Equation (8) of Bhat Kapu and Kiruthika (2024) when each observation is assigned to its largest membership. If all weights are zero, the fuzzy average is undefined (NaN) and a warning is given.

If average = "median", the median width is reported.

Missing widths are removed before averaging.

References

Bhat Kapu, S., & Kiruthika. (2024). Some density-based silhouette diagnostics for soft clustering algorithms. Communications in Statistics: Case Studies, Data Analysis and Applications, 10(3-4), 221-238. doi:10.1080/23737484.2024.2408534

See also

Silhouette, softSilhouette, dbSilhouette, calSilhouette, getSilhouette, is.Silhouette, plotSilhouette

Examples

prob <- matrix(c(0.90, 0.10,
                 0.60, 0.40,
                 0.20, 0.80,
                 0.45, 0.55), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
cerSilhouette(prob)
#>   cluster neighbor sil_width
#> 1       1        2      0.90
#> 2       1        2      0.60
#> 3       2        1      0.80
#> 4       2        1      0.55

# \donttest{
# Compare two soft clustering algorithms on the iris data
data(iris)
if (requireNamespace("ppclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fcm_result <- ppclust::fcm(iris[, 1:4], 3)
  out_fcm <- cerSilhouette(prob_matrix = fcm_result$u, print.summary = TRUE)
  plot(out_fcm)
  fcm2_result <- ppclust::fcm2(iris[, 1:4], 3)
  out_fcm2 <- cerSilhouette(prob_matrix = fcm2_result$u)
  c(fcm = summary(out_fcm, print.summary = FALSE)$avg.width,
    fcm2 = summary(out_fcm2, print.summary = FALSE)$avg.width)
} else {
  message("Install 'ppclust' to run this example: install.packages('ppclust')")
}
#> -----------------------------------------------------
#> Average crisp similarity certainty silhouette: 0.8572
#> -----------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>  cluster size avg.sil.width
#>        1   50        0.9645
#>        2   40        0.8351
#>        3   60        0.7826
#>       fcm      fcm2 
#> 0.8572481 0.6235972 
# }
